summary: Nancy Hatch Dupree was a history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. She studied at Barnard College (~1945–1949) and Columbia University (~1950–1953), later holding a post at Kabul University (~2006–2017).

Nancy Hock specialized in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of California, Berkeley (1987) under Joanna Gottfried Williams, Lewis Lancaster, Eugene F. Irschick, and Barend A. van Nooten, and was affiliated with the Asian Art Museum in 1987.

Nancy McCagney worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She studied under Chögyam Trungpa, Ninian Smart, Gerald James Larson, William F. Powell, and Andrew Rawlinson, and held a post at the University of Delaware (attested 1997).

Nandini Bhattacharyya-Panda is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. She served as a Senior Fellow at the Indian Council of Historical Research and as a Project Fellow at the Maulana Abul Kalam Azad Institute of Asian Studies (attested 2011).
Nang Dzé Drubpé Dorjé studied under Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Shechen Gyaltsab.

Nanigopal Majumdar worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Superintendent for the Archaeological Survey of India (1931) and as Superintendent of the Archaeological Section at the Indian Museum, Kolkata (attested 1939).
Nantu Shaw is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. Shaw was a Visiting Scholar at Stony Brook University and studied under doctoral supervisor Sthaneshwar Timalsina (both attested 2026).

Naoji Okuyama is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He completed doctoral coursework at Tohoku University (~1980–1985), where he worked as an assistant and lecturer (~1985–1993), before serving as professor at Koyasan University (~2000, attested 2026).
Naoki Nabeshima specializes in Buddhist studies. In 2004, he was attested as Professor of Shin Buddhist Studies at Ryukoku University and is recorded as having founded the university.

Naoko Nishimura specializes in Indology and linguistics. She completed her PhD at Tohoku University (1993–2002) under Toshifumi Goto, Hirofumi Isoda, and Shinkan Murakami, and later served there as a specialist researcher (attested 2026).

Naomi Appleton works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. She earned her D.Phil. at Oxford under Christopher Minkowski and David Gellner, was a British Academy Postdoctoral Fellow at Cardiff University, and became professor and Co-Director at the University of Edinburgh.
Naomi Worth studied Tibetology and religious studies at the University of Virginia, where she also held a post (attested 2018).
Naomichi Nakada is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied under Ram Chandra Pandeya and doctoral supervisor Vasudev Vishwanath Gokhale.

Naoshiro Tsuji was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Tokyo and Oxford. He served as Chair of Sanskrit at the University of Tokyo (1942–1960), professor at Keio University (1960), and director of Toyo Bunko (1974).
Naoya Funahashi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who held posts at Otani University (attested 1981) and as a research fellow at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science.
Narada Maha Thera was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. Educated at St. Benedict's College and University College, Colombo, he served as Superior of Vajiraramaya Temple (~1955–1983).

Narayan Hemandas Samtani was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He earned his PhD at the University of Delhi (1957–1961) under Vasudev Vishwanath Gokhale and served as Lecturer in Pali at Banaras Hindu University (~1961–1984).
Narayana Shastri Khiste was an Indology scholar who served as Librarian at Sarasvati Bhavana Library (attested 1932) and Principal at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1950).
Narendra Nath Bhattacharyya was a scholar of history, archaeology, religious studies, and Indology. He held a post at the University of Calcutta from approximately 1967 to 1999.

Narendrachandra Bhattacharyya was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He served as General Editor of the Calcutta Sanskrit Series (attested 1936) and as a Pandit at the University of Calcutta (attested 1943).
